items.stem: Why do machine-learning teams keep a separate 'test' dataset?

options.text: To measure how well the model performs on data it has not seen during training
options.rationale: Correct: test data estimates real-world generalisation.

options.text: To give the model more examples to memorise
options.rationale: Test data is held back precisely so it is not memorised.

options.text: Because training data is always wrong
options.rationale: Training data is used to learn; test data checks generalisation.

options.text: To make training take longer on purpose
options.rationale: The purpose is honest evaluation, not slowing training.

items.explanation: Correct: test data estimates real-world generalisation.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO signs suggest a model is overfitting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Very high accuracy on training data
options.rationale: Correct: near-perfect training scores can indicate memorisation.

options.text: Much lower accuracy on new test data
options.rationale: Correct: a big train-test gap is a classic overfitting sign.

options.text: Equal and reasonable accuracy on train and test
options.rationale: Similar scores suggest healthy generalisation, not overfitting.
Without training data the model has not learned yet; that is not overfitting.

items.explanation: Correct: near-perfect training scores can indicate memorisation.

items.stem: A spam classifier scores 99% on training data but 60% on new messages. What is the likely issue?

options.text: It has overfit the training data and does not generalise to new messages
options.rationale: Correct: a large train-test gap points to overfitting.

options.text: It is the best possible model
options.rationale: A large gap shows it is not generalising well.
The test data is exactly what revealed the problem.

options.text: The model has learned nothing at all
options.rationale: It learned the training set too closely, which is overfitting.

items.explanation: Correct: a large train-test gap points to overfitting.
